Add to that row what this review measured: the parked population has grown from 5 permission-gate skips to 11, all unresolved, and 9 of them promise a 'prep' unblock with prep_prompt NULL -- so whichever shape is built must also fill prep_prompt, or the attended pass still arrives with nothing to run. **Fact:** **P10 - Tooling.** USE CASE: four runner lane routines (deepbench-runner, lanes 2-4) fire on staggered 3-hour crons so tickets can build in parallel (AGT-265). Before building, runner_should_boot() compares live lanes to runner_settings.max_lanes, which is a FIXED value (1) that no job ever changes — only runner_should_boot() reads it, and the only writes in the repo are test fixtures that set it

**Proposed resolution:** Rule this ticket, and the ruling lands on the ticket: root-cause with reuse_backlog_id = this ticket's own id plus a project HOMES it (general leaves it where it is and is itself the ruling); root-cause with reuse_backlog_id naming another open ticket SUPERSEDES it; not-a-defect CLOSES it with your reason; list parks it when the fitting project's list is locked; escalate with john_call rules when only John can decide. Never root-cause without reuse_backlog_id and never cleanup -- the ticket exists, so a second one is refused.

**Ruling:** AGT-608 is john-named (backlog_items.scope_origin, read live) and sits in epic Tooling under project tooling, status executing with BOTH its epics locked -- so a filing group routing into it is refused twice over under AGT-240, and I never close or supersede a john-named ticket.
